private.name: Reflection AI

data.narrative:
Alpha School is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company founded by MacKenzie Price and Brian Holtz. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers, supplemented by reference to a broader set of nine private and one public company (Palantir) operating in the AI and software sector.

The peer-median method was applied as the primary triangulation approach. The five direct comparables—Scale AI ($29.0B Series B), Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B Series B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B Series B), and Field AI ($2.0B Series B)—yield a median valuation of $5.6B. This method reflects the wide dispersion present in frontier-stage AI valuations, with the peer set ranging from $2.0B at the low end to $29.0B at the high end.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4.8B to $6.4B, with a median point estimate of $5.6B. Key uncertainties include the applicability of comparables operating at Series B stage to an earlier-stage company, the absence of granular operational metrics across the peer set, and the sector's sensitivity to capital availability and narrative momentum. A single triangulation method limits confidence; additional revenue or profitability-based approaches would strengthen conviction.
